messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — saw client X spike candidate counts to ~12k for a single rerank request, caused visible backpressure across ranking pool
Alex: yikes. any 429s or queueing observed?
Maya: no 429s early — latency climbed and we hit per-model inflight cap; downstream queues grew
Sam: can we add a candidate-reservation/unit accounting before fanout? reserve N 'candidate-units' at admission to avoid oversubscribe
Liz: +1 for admission control. need telemetry dims for reservation_granted, reservation_rejected, reservation_used
Keegan: console UX idea: per-project 'candidate budget' slider + opt-in enforcement toggle (soft vs hard). show estimated token-cost and worst-case latency
Alex: implementation sketch — candidate_unit = ceil(tokens/64) * model_cost_factor; reserve sum(cu) at admission. if reserve fails, fallback to partial_results or model_fanout->cheaper models
Maya: partial results ok for some; SLAs need hard-fail option
Sam: pseudo-request shape for proposer API:
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "candidates": [{"id":"c1","text":"..."}, ...],
  "budget": {"units": 500, "mode": "best-effort"},
  "model_affinity": "latency-optimized"
}
```
Alex: budget.mode enum: "best-effort", "strict", "fallback"
Liz: telemetry names we'd add: rerank.candidate_units.requested, rerank.candidate_units.reserved, rerank.candidate_units.rejected, rerank.fallback.path (enum: none, partial, cheaper_model, 429). Tag with tenant, route, model_version
Keegan: for console charting: show candidate-unit consumption over time + expected latency overlay; alert when p95 latency > X or reservation_reject_rate > 1%
Maya: model selection tie-in — if affinity allowed, routing can target cheaper 8-bit quantized variant when budget low. need contract that cheaper variant supports same output shape
Sam: propose model compatibility metadata: supports_shape=true, max_candidates=N, token_scale=0.25
Alex: backward compat: add header `X-Used-Candidate-Units: 123` in response so clients can measure hit-to-budget
Keegan: rollout plan: canary reservation in infra for 5% traffic; console soft-limit slider for early-access tenants; telemetry sampling 100% candidate_units, detailed fallback reasons at 10%
Sam: need graceful degradation in router: on reservation fail, try descending model-tier list, preemptive cache checks to reuse scores
Maya: QA: unit test compute_candidate_units, e2e scaled fanout, perf run with 10k candidate traces
Alex: note — batching heuristics should still combine candidates across requests if model_affinity matches; reservation must be per-tenant
Liz: observability TODOs: dashboard panels (per-tenant candidate_units, per-model inflight, reservation_reject_rate), log samples when fallback triggers with sample_id
Keegan: UX TODOs: show 'why my rerank was partial' toast in console with link to docs and recommended budget
Maya: decision check: soft default (best-effort) for self-serve, strict for enterprise? seems reasonable
Sam: +1, allow policy override via tenant config (enforced by control plane)
Alex: I'll draft API Proto change and migration doc. RFC in #eng-platform tomorrow
InfraBot: canary deploy queued: rerank-reservation-v0.1 -> staging at 1745123480
Maya: thanks — RFC should include telemetry schema, console mocks, fallback semantics
Liz: will add dashboard skeleton and sample queries
Keegan: I'll prototype slider UI and add copy for partial-results tooltip
Sam: I'll add admission control + unit accounting to router branch and test locally
Maya: cool. follow-ups: Alex write RFC, Sam open infra PR, Keegan mockup, Liz dashboard. pinging @all for visibility :eyes:
